newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Mark unsteady, French markets head higher.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Mark unsteady, French markets head higher.

text.p: The mark was unsettled in European morning trading on Tuesday, amid concern that a single European currency would not match it for strength, but later revived a little against the dollar.
French stocks added to the previous day's surprise gains as investors and traders gave the new Socialist-led government the benefit of the doubt while awaiting details of its programme.
"The market's taking a gamble, giving credit to (Prime Minister Lionel) Jospin that he will not shake up Europe and, as the (stock) market is cheap, people are buying," a Paris share trader said.

The franc and bonds were also higher. The French currency had hit a low for the year of 3.3860 per mark after the weekend election results but a slide in the German currency propelled it back towards 3.37.
Elsewhere, the London stock market retreated as banks turned mixed after an initial rebound, while Frankfurt was higher.

Market perceptions that the left's victory in the French parliamentary elections could lead to broad membership of a euro currency from the planned 1999 start helped the dollar hit a morning high of 1.7330 marks. It later slipped back by around a pfennig.
Socialist Elisabeth Guigou, tipped for office in the new Paris government, said her party would respect the start date for European economic and monetary union.

Traders said if a broadly-based euro was launched on time without really tough measures to back it, rather than a delay which could prompt funds to flood back into the mark, it would be good news for the dollar.

"We know the Socialists want to go ahead on time but we know they're not so committed to actually meeting the criteria themselves -- that's underpinning the dollar," said Thomas Rayner, international economist at SGST.
But some currency analysts said the market could be underestimating the chances of a delay.

"The conflicts and inconsistencies in this whole project have never looked greater. The risk for the market is that prospects for delay are not treated seriously enough," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy in London.

Traders said the dollar's fall through support around 1.7260 marks sparked stop-loss selling, while it was also jolted by a meeting between Bundesbank head Hans Tietmeyer and Finance Minister Theo Waigel.
A row between the Bundesbank and Bonn over plans to revalue the central bank's assets to help Germany qualify for EMU has undermined the German currency.
After the meeting, Waigel and Tietmeyer said they were on the way to reaching agreement on the plans to revalue gold and currency reserves.

A decline in the dollar against the yen also affected the dollar/mark rate. Currency traders said the Japanese currency, along with the pound and Swiss franc, was gaining from a search for safe havens.
U.S. April leading indicators figures are due at 1400 GMT but the main market focus is on May non-farm payrolls data on Friday.
If payrolls are strong, they would boost market expectations of higher U.S. interest rates at the next Federal Reserve policy-making meeting in July. But many economists have cut their forecasts.

French shares followed Monday's rollercoaster ride with early gains of around one percent as the previous day's biggest losers, banking shares and privatisation stocks, rebounded and bonds gained. But the bourse traded below its highs by the end of the morning.
The London stock market, Europe's biggest, opened steady, with a weak overnight performance on Wall Street countered by higher bonds and a revival in bank shares.
But it later slipped on interest rate fears ahead of a key British central bank monetary meeting on Thursday and the U.S. jobs data.
"With Wall Street easier, uncertainty about rates ahead of the (monetary) meeting later this week and the budget coming up on July 2, we're bound for a setback," said one senior dealer.
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones industrial average fell 41.64 points to 7,289.40 on Monday as investors sold blue chips to buy smaller companies and bonds rose.
The Tokyo stock market's key Nikkei average closed at a new high for 1997, up 111.31 points or 0.54 percent at 20,563.16.
CURRENCIES AT 1145 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7235 marks and 115.80 yen, compared with 1.7266 and 116.63 in late European trading on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1145 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index was down 32.7 points or 0.72 percent at 4,530.1.
PARIS - The CAC 40 was up 17.13 points or 0.66 percent at 2,618.58.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended floor trade up 20.12 points or 0.56 percent at 3,625.74.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold traded around $344.30 an ounce, compared with the previous London close of $344.05. Silver was one cent firmer at $4.76.
